history.rationale: Corresponds to standard position V507I, a canonical m102.4 escape mutation where side-chain steric bulk selectively disrupts antibody binding while maintaining ephrin-B2/B3 engagement.
Structurally very conservative, but lower predicted escape compared to positions 460-485 lowers priority.
Corresponds to standard position D555N; abolishes the critical salt bridge with m102.4 heavy chain CDR while preserving receptor-binding capability.
Shows exceptional antibody escape potential in evescape alongside positive backbone stability in ProteinMPNN.
Conservative charge preservation with extended side-chain length at standard D555 to induce steric clashes in the tight m102.4 paratope pocket.
Significantly penalized by ProteinMPNN delta relative to the superior D485N substitution.
Corresponds to standard position Q530K at the antibody-receptor interface; introduces positive charge and steric hindrance disrupting m102.4 CDR contacts.
High predicted escape combined with favorable ProteinMPNN conditional probability supports top-tier ranking.
Corresponds to standard Q530A; removes key hydrogen-bonding interactions with m102.4 while retaining overall fold and receptor engagement.
High escape score is tempered by noticeably unfavorable structural compatibility delta.
Corresponds to standard position E533Q; neutralizes negative charge that coordinates m102.4 paratope basic residues, reducing antibody neutralization.
Possesses near-optimal structural compatibility and solid escape score, serving as a reliable alternative at position 463.
Charge-reversal at standard E533 designed to create electrostatic repulsion against m102.4 basic residues in CDR-H3.
Demonstrates high escape prediction and outstanding structural compatibility on the Nipah G backbone.
Alternative hydrophobic extension at standard V507 to sterically perturb m102.4 binding without destabilizing the hydrophobic core of the binding face.
Underperforms on both escape potential and fixed-backbone structural compatibility.
Corresponds to standard T531A; eliminates antibody-specific hydrogen bonding at the periphery of the ephrin-binding surface.
Provides strong escape while maintaining neutral structural compatibility.
Corresponds to standard N557D; alters the local electrostatic potential adjacent to the m102.4 contact surface to favor immune escape.
Moderate escape score and acceptable structural tolerance maintain viability in the middle pool.
